Subject: Triage update — pacing regression traced to model variant rollout (edge cache miss storm)

Alex, Karthik — quick triage update from engineering:

What we observed:
- At ~08:48 PT we saw an increase in tail latency on streaming endpoints serving the US-west region.
- Root cause: an automated model variant rollout changed a small percentage of traffic to a variant that exhibits cold-KV-cache behavior for certain prompt families. That coupled with a large influx of new sessions (Fjord traffic spike) caused a high rate of KV cache misses and increased synchronous per-token compute for the first 60–90 tokens.

Impact:
- New sessions routed to affected variant experienced 600–1,300ms per token for the first ~50 tokens; warmed sessions dropped back to baseline. Estimated impact window: 08:48–09:20 PT.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:35 PT):
- Rolled back the variant rollout (stop and revert on affected pool).
- Increased the prefetch threshold for KV cache warming on US-west edge pool.
- Enabled temporary per-session token pacing (soft limit) to reduce amplification during warmup.

Attachments: diagnostic_trace_20260623.txt (contains anonymized trace + kernel selection samples)

Next steps (tracking):
- Engineering will run synthetic warmup tasks to validate prefetch changes and monitor tail latency for 24h. Owner: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
- Product will schedule a guardrail to prevent automatic rollout to variants without a warmup profile. Owner: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai (ETA: 2026-07-02)

Alex — short term, you should see median token pacing return to normal within 10–20 minutes of rollback; we’ll keep you posted on the post-incident report and longer-term fixes. We’ll also share any recommended client-side knobs if you want to harden for future warmup behavior.

— Marissa

Alex / Fjord team — thanks again for your patience while we completed the initial analysis. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the actions we’re taking. I’ve attached the full postmortem and a recovery playbook for your ops team.

Executive summary:
- Incident: transient high token-level latency (pacing regression) on live streaming/chat endpoints impacting US-west (edge pool 12).
- Impact window: 2026-06-23 08:48 PT through 2026-06-23 09:20 PT (root-cause window ~32 minutes).
- Customers impacted: subset of new sessions for Fjord Health routed to the variant during an automatic rollout. You reported the issue at 09:15 PT.

Root cause:
- Automated model variant rollout exposed a variant lacking robust KV-cache-warmup behavior. A concurrent traffic spike amplified KV cache miss rate, causing synchronous per-token compute on cold paths and increasing per-token latencies.

What we did (mitigations):
- Immediate rollback of rollout at 09:35 PT.
- Increased KV cache prefetch thresholds and introduced synthetic warmup tasks for variants.
- Temporary per-session token pacing to reduce amplification until warmup completes.

Permanent remediation & timeline:
- Guardrail: disallow automated rollout for variants without warmup profiles (owner: tessa_morgan, ETA: 2026-07-02).
- Platform enhancement: automated synthetic warmup as part of rollout pipeline (owner: marissa_cole, ETA: 2026-07-16).
- Observability: add a rollout-effect dashboard and a rule to halt rollouts if edge-pool tail latency increases > 2x baseline (owner: marissa_cole, ETA: 2026-06-30).

Client recommendations (short-term runbook items):
- If you operate a client-side session router, prefer sticky sessions to warmed edge pools during deployments.
- Implement a small client warmup (2–3 short synthetic prompts) prior to clinician handoff for high-sensitivity flows.
- Configure an exponential backoff for retrying streaming connections to avoid amplification during rollout windows.

SLA / credits and next steps:
- I’ve started a procurement ticket (HubSpot HS-78932) — we’ll evaluate impact-based SLA credit per our agreement and follow up with the finance team. Procurement@redwood will reach out if additional paperwork is required.
